mainEntity.name: What are leading lines in photography?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Leading lines are lines within a photograph that can suggest

direction, connect elements or create a sense of depth.

They may draw attention towards a subject or encourage

exploration of the wider scene. Their effect depends on

the whole composition and how the viewer responds to it.

mainEntity.name: What are examples of leading lines?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Roads, rivers, footpaths, fences, shorelines, shadows and

building edges can all form leading lines. For example,

a winding path may connect a nearby walker with distant

hills. Consider what the line contributes to the scene

before deciding how prominently to include it.

mainEntity.name: What are the main types of leading lines?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Common types include horizontal, vertical, diagonal,

curved and converging lines. A photograph can also

contain implied pathways, such as repeated shapes or

a person's gaze. These categories describe possibilities;

the light, subject and surrounding space influence

what each pathway communicates.

mainEntity.name: How do you use leading lines in a photograph?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Begin with what interests you in the scene. Look for

lines that connect, separate or emphasise its elements,

then compare viewpoints and framing. Make one version

with the pathway prominent and another with it reduced.

Choose the photograph that best expresses your intention.

mainEntity.name: Do leading lines have to end at the subject?

acceptedAnswer.text:
No. A subject near the end of a line can create a clear

connection, but it can also sit beside or partway along

the line. A pathway may suggest distance, movement or

a relationship between several elements without ending

at a single subject.

mainEntity.name: Can leading lines go out of the frame?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes. A line continuing beyond the frame can suggest

movement or a larger world outside the photograph.

Change it when it creates an unwanted distraction.

Judge its contribution to the whole image rather than

treating every line that crosses an edge as a mistake.

mainEntity.name: Do you need a wide-angle lens for leading lines?

acceptedAnswer.text:
No. Leading lines can be photographed with a phone or

different camera lenses. A wide-angle lens lets you

include more of the scene and work close to a foreground

line. Camera position affects perspective, so compare

how the line relates to the background from different

positions.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between leading lines and visual pathways?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Leading lines are one kind of visual pathway. I use

visual pathways as a broader term that includes lines,

changes in light, repeated shapes, gestures and gaze.

These can suggest connections within a photograph

without forming a continuous line or guaranteeing

where someone will look.
